subject: Control/Data bridge — segmentation, NAT options, and ops handback
messages:
From: Nicholas Reed <nreed@edgeworks.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: EdgeWorks Systems Eng Team <eng@edgeworks.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment: control/data separation and egress patterns

Alex —

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. We’re evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for a sensitive inference workload and want to validate the control/data plane bridge pattern before committing to a Dedicated environment. A few items we need clarity on: 

- Control plane reachability: we want the control plane APIs to be reachable from our on-prem racks but not expose management plane egress to the public internet. What are recommended patterns (reverse tunnel, S2S VPN, private link)?
- Data plane egress: model downloads and OS package updates need internet egress for a handful of maintenance tasks — we need a deterministic NAT strategy that fits our compliance rules (no wide-open internet egress from runtime hosts).
- Segmentation: ensure runtime (data plane) cannot initiate lateral control plane connections except via authenticated, mutual TLS channels.
- Ops handback: after POC we expect a gradual handback of on-call and runbook ownership. We need to know what artifacts (runbooks, playbooks, SLOs) Redwood provides.

I’ve attached our internal topology PDF (edgeworks-internal-topology.pdf) for context. Can you propose a deployment pattern and an operations handoff checklist? 

—Nick
Nicholas Reed
Head of Infrastructure
EdgeWorks Systems

Attachments: edgeworks-internal-topology.pdf (diagram)
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Nicholas Reed <nreed@edgeworks.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks Systems Eng Team <eng@edgeworks.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 18:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: control/data separation and egress patterns

Nick — thanks for the topology and the clear list. High level proposal below; I’ll loop in our network/ops SME for details and a short design sketch.

Summary proposal (short):
- Control plane connectivity: we recommend a private, customer-initiated VPN (IPsec or WireGuard) with mutual auth to Redwood’s management endpoints, or AWS PrivateLink for customers who want fully private control-plane RPCs. For on-prem racks, the same VPN approach works; we support persistent tunnels and health checks.
- Control/data segmentation: control-plane components (config, rollout APIs, control traffic) should live in a separate management subnet with strict SGs/ACLs. Data-plane inference nodes are in dedicated runtime subnets. Only an authenticated northbound mTLS channel from runtime -> control is allowed (no inbound admin SSH).
- Egress/NAT options (choose one):
  1) Centralized NAT gateway (recommended): single egress NAT in a controlled subnet with egress firewall rules, proxy for OS updates. Allows audit and egress whitelisting.
  2) Per-subnet NAT with NAT instances: provides better isolation per tenant but higher ops overhead.
  3) Redwood-managed egress proxy (partner pattern): runtime nodes route outbound to a Redwood-managed proxy over the private tunnel; Redwood performs outbound fetches and returns artifacts — reduces customer egress footprint but requires an explicit contract.

- Ops handback: we provide a POC runbook, playbooks for canary rollback, an acceptance checklist, and a 4-week joint run period where Redwood retains incident response for Tier 2. Post handback you’ll own on-call; we’ll remain second-line for 90 days.

I’ve put a compact reference sketch and a one-pager in the attached PDF: redwood-control-data-bridge-proposal.pdf and a quick PNG sketch for your diagram pool.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which egress pattern you prefer (centralized NAT / per-subnet / Redwood proxy).
2) If centralized NAT, share the egress firewall whitelist we should allow for model downloads (I’ve included the model fetch FQDNs in the proposal).
3) Schedule a 45m deep-dive with our networking SME (kimberly_park) to lock down BGP/route-reflectors if you want BGP-based transit.

Happy to jump on a call — propose Wed 30th 10:00 AM ET?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-control-data-bridge-proposal.pdf, redwood-vpc-reference-sketch.png
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Private deployment: control/data separation and egress patterns (technical clarifications)

Alex / team — quick tech items we should confirm before the Wed deep-dive: 

1) BGP vs static: If EdgeWorks wants BGP for their transit, we need AS prep and route filters on both sides. Confirm if they need prefix propagation for model artifact CDN IPs or whether we should keep those on the customer NAT whitelist.
2) MTU and TCP MSS clamping: on-prem racks + IPsec tunnels often have MTU issues. Recommend MSS clamp on the NAT gateway or allow jumbo MTU inside the fabric if available.
3) Hairpinning and internal fetches: central NAT must support hairpin (SNAT) for cases where runtime nodes fetch artifacts that resolve to public IPs owned by EdgeWorks. 
4) TLS termination: all control RPCs are mTLS; do not terminate TLS at our proxy unless explicitly agreed. If they require TLS interception for deep inspection, that’s a compliance conversation with legal.
5) KMS & secrets: confirm if EdgeWorks will use their KMS (customer-managed) for runtime secrets or if they prefer Redwood KMS with a customer HSM-backed key. This changes the network path for key-rolls.

Operational suggestions for POC:
- Provide an 'egress whitelist' template we can pre-fill (includes model fetch origins, package repos, monitoring endpoints).
- Agree SAML/SCIM for user mapping and a short-lived service account for the POC.
- Collect contact list and AWS account IDs (or on-prem VPN endpoints) prior to the deep-dive.

Jonas — can you review the NAT nuances for per-tenant SNAT vs centralized SNAT and add anything I missed?

—Kim

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Nicholas Reed <nreed@edgeworks.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks Systems Eng Team <eng@edgeworks.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: control/data separation and egress patterns

Nick — thanks again. Quick summary and proposed schedule so we’re aligned: 

What we agreed (summary):
- Control plane: customer-initiated IPsec/WireGuard VPN from EdgeWorks to Redwood management endpoints. Mutual mTLS for all management RPCs.
- Segmentation: control plane in management subnet, runtime in isolated subnets. No admin inbound to runtime; runtime may initiate authenticated control RPCs only.
- Egress: EdgeWorks preference = centralized NAT gateway with egress firewall. We’ll provide a whitelist template and pre-seed the known model/package origins.
- Ops handback: Redwood supplies POC runbook, acceptance checklist, and 4-week joint run period followed by a formal handback.

Action items: 
1) EdgeWorks: share egress firewall whitelist and VPN endpoints (public IP + shared pre-shared key if using IPsec) by Thu 07/02.
2) Redwood (me + Kim + Jonas): deliver a revised proposal PDF with explicit BGP/MTU recommendations and a NAT test plan by Fri 07/03. (See attached proposal PDF and sketch).
3) Schedule POC kickoff: Wed 07/07 10:00 AM ET — 45m. Confirm availability.

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short Teams link. Feel free to reply with any immediate concerns.

Best regards,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
